body.statement: Open-ended Question 7. Determine the limiting minimax power function when \(r^{1/4}\sqrt{\delta_{\mathrm{sq}}}\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\), and decide whether an exactly calibrated quadratic minimizer attains it among \(\Psi_{\alpha,r}\). If not, characterize the strict gain of a nonquadratic invariant test.
body.justification: Rate optimality does not decide whether quadratic compression loses a motif-specific power constant.
body.gap: No cited source derives the finite invariant composite testing experiment needed for exact procedural optimality.
body.consumer: The answer determines whether a platform should deploy a more complex motif-likelihood test.

obligation.what_is_open: Identification of the sharp local asymptotic experiment and its minimax power envelope, followed by comparison of that envelope with the exactly calibrated quadratic statistic.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen orbit handle names a quotient construction but supplies neither limiting null and alternative likelihood kernels nor a uniform reduction of the copy-specific composite nuisance schedules to a tensor experiment. The Hellinger comparison proves contiguity-scale impossibility but does not yield likelihood-ratio convergence or a least-favourable prior that is sharp in constant.
obligation.attempted: The symmetric compact-shift prior was tensorized and its fourth-order Hellinger information was computed exactly. This yields the all-test lower constant, but affinity alone does not identify the limiting power curve. The finite motif orbit reduction was also considered, but arbitrary legal nuisance blocks may vary across copies, so an iid orbit-likelihood limit cannot be asserted from the present primitives.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved results determine the minimax local rate and the explicit bracket
\[
\sqrt{1-\alpha-\eta}\,L_H(V_r^{\mathrm{quad}})^{1/4}
\le r^*_{\alpha,\eta}(H,r)
\le\{\alpha^{-1/2}+\eta^{-1/2}\}^{1/2}(V_r^{\mathrm{quad}})^{1/4}.
\]
Equivalently, they give nontrivial upper and lower power controls on every sequence for which \(r^{1/4}\sqrt{\delta_{\mathrm{sq}}}\) stays bounded, but they do not identify a common limiting experiment or a sharp limiting power function.
